arc: Man in a hole: the last ice leaves a dock that is running out (0, quiet), a choice of buoys while the Quay rations water (-1), the buoy is lit and the first lamp goes on (+2, a false peak), the flare comes three weeks early (-2), Ilse will not leave her dock (-3), her channel goes to static (-3, the bottom at 0.83), Lamp Quay and its second lamp (+1, bittersweet).
note: Scenes open in src/voyage.c at fixed progress points (the start of the run and the end of each of the five legs); the words are in web/app.js. The integrator in src/orbit.c is unchanged; story beats change only the fuel in the tank, the target rings, how much the apsis readout wobbles, the flare's boil-off and what a tow costs. The actual order per seed is in play-order.json, story numbers on/off and per choice path in ablation.json, per-leg crises and failures in tension.json, all written by make story. tests/test_voyage.c checks the order, every [mech] number, the [quiet] heavy scenes and both choices; make test re-runs bench rows and requires them verbatim. Emotion values were re-scored on 2026-11-02 by a reviewer who is not the author (dock 0, flare -2, silence -3, quay +1).

characters.want: keep the inner dock's pumps turning until the last ice is out
characters.need: to let someone else carry it the rest of the way
characters.start: will not leave her dock; counts every burn for the pilot
characters.end: stays with the dock in the flare; her count goes to static and the pilot counts alone

characters.want: every tank home and a lamp lit for each one
characters.need: to accept that not everyone comes back
characters.start: promises a lamp for every tank that comes home
characters.end: lights the second lamp for someone who is not coming

beats.summary: The inner dock's last shift. Ilse puts in what fuel the dock can spare (0.30 to 0.40), keeps the reserve pod, sets the rule (two burns, not three) and says she will call the burns, which steadies the readout.
beats.evidence: Lamp Quay drinks it or nobody does.

beats.summary: Pell: the Quay's tanks are below the marks, the children are on half cups. Two buoys are lit: Lark is close but drained; Wick is far up the well and its keeper will fire spare fuel down.

labels: Make for Lark, the near buoy (short climb)
Climb to Wick, the far buoy (long climb, fuel sent down)

beats.evidence: Close is quick. Far is fuel.

beats.summary: The buoy is lit and the tug is a real blip on the Quay's board. Pell lights the first lamp, one for every tank that comes home. What is left in the buoy's cache goes into the tank.
beats.evidence: I'm lighting the first lamp on the Quay.

beats.summary: The flare season comes three weeks early. Pell shouts; Ilse sends the tug below the front and warns that when it arrives the tank will boil off and the readout will jump.

The dock is inside the flare. Ilse will not leave: the pumps need a hand. She has sent the reserve pod down to a lower ring. Pell begs; Ilse answers 'Count the cups.' Turn back for the pod (a detour and a wait) or hold the heading.

labels: Turn back for her pod (a detour, then a wait while it pumps)
Hold the heading for Lamp Quay

beats.evidence: I'm not coming. The pumps need a hand on them

beats.summary: Ilse's last words break off and the channel goes to static. Nobody steadies the readout now, and a dry tank brings Lamp Quay's tug, which drags you back to the start of the leg. You say her rule to nobody.
beats.evidence: The channel hisses. Nobody calls the next burn.

beats.summary: Lamp Quay takes the ice. Pell lights the second lamp; the ending depends on whether you turned back for Ilse's pod.
beats.evidence: Lamp Quay takes your hold of ice.

text: Lamp Quay takes your hold of ice. Pell meets you at the lock with a lamp in each hand.
Ilse's empty pod is still clamped to your hull. You can repeat every word she said on the way down to it.
Lamp Quay takes your hold of ice. You came in early, and the kids get full cups tonight.
Pell lights the second lamp and doesn't say anything for a long time.
Your log has her last call cut off in the middle of a word, somewhere behind you in the static. You count your own burns now.
